unit.title: Comparatives
unit.subtitle: More than, less than, and as… as

grammar.title: Compare anything: taller, cheaper, as fast as
grammar.intro: To compare two things in Spanish you slot an adjective into a fixed frame: más … que (more than), menos … que (less than), or tan … como (as … as). A few common adjectives break the pattern with their own words: mejor, peor, mayor, menor.

sections.heading: More than: más + adjective + que
sections.body: Put the adjective between más and que. The adjective still agrees with the first thing:

ex.es: El tren es más rápido que el bus.
ex.en: The train is faster than the bus.

sections.heading: Less than: menos + adjective + que
sections.body: Same frame, but with menos to say something has less of a quality:

ex.es: Este coche es menos caro que el otro.
ex.en: This car is less expensive than the other.
Today I'm less tired than yesterday.

sections.heading: As … as: tan + adjective + como
sections.body: For equality use tan … como with an adjective. Careful: it's como, not que. For equal quantities of a noun, use tanto/a/os/as … como, agreeing with the noun:

ex.en: Luis is as tall as Ana.
I have as many books as you.

sections.heading: Irregular comparatives
sections.body: Four adjectives have their own comparative word — don't say “más bueno” or “más malo”:

ex.es: Este café es mejor que el otro.
ex.en: This coffee is better than the other.
My brother is older than me.

takeaways: tanto/a/os/as + noun + como = as much/many … as.
Irregulars: mejor, peor, mayor, menor — never 'más bueno'.

mistakes.w: Este vino es más bueno que el otro.
mistakes.r: Este vino es mejor que el otro.
mistakes.why: 'bueno' has an irregular comparative: mejor, not 'más bueno'.

mistakes.w: Ana es tan alta que Luis.
mistakes.r: Ana es tan alta como Luis.
mistakes.why: With 'tan' the second word is 'como', not 'que'.
Before a noun use tanto/a/os/as (here tantos), not 'tan'.

exercises.no: For 'more than' use más … que: “más alta que”.

exercises.prompt: Este café es ___ que el otro.
exercises.prompt_en: This coffee is better than the other.

exercises.prompt: Build: “Luis is as tall as Ana.”
exercises.no: Equality uses tan … como: “Luis es tan alto como Ana.”

exercises.prompt_en: My brother is older than me.
exercises.no: Older → “mayor”: “Mi hermano es mayor que yo.”

exercises.prompt: Match each English comparative to its Spanish word.

exercises.tts: El tren es más rápido que el autobús.
accepted: el tren es mas rapido que el autobus
exercises.translation: The train is faster than the bus.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “El tren es más rápido que el autobús.”
exercises.no: It was: “El tren es más rápido que el autobús.” (The train is faster than the bus.)

exercises.scenario: Comparing two phones in a shop 📱

options.text: Sí, es mejor que el otro.
Sí, es más bueno que el otro.
Sí, es tan mejor que el otro.
